posts.text:
Rural Healthcare is essential to Hawaiʻi's communities, and protecting it takes work.

I was glad to join the Hawaiʻi Health Systems Corporation All Boards Meeting during National Rural Health Month, to talk story and discuss the year ahead-from protecting Medicaid and securing https://t.co/GyEc6unNdl

Gas prices in Hawaiʻi have skyrocketed to an average of $5.63 a gallon as the war in Iran drives up costs. Families can’t fill their gas tanks with promises.

I’m calling on Congress to suspend the federal gas tax and finally bring relief at the pump. The time to act is NOW. https://t.co/qU3hbzjIuA

Gas prices in Hawaiʻi have skyrocketed to an average of $5.63 a gallon as the war in Iran drives up costs. Families can’t fill their gas tanks with promises.

I’m calling on Congress to suspend the federal gas tax and finally bring relief at the pump. The time to act is NOW. https://t.co/bjTIqdt4cV

Congress is back, and we’ve got work to do.

Major funding decisions are on the table, important legislation remains unfinished, and we can’t afford to waste a single day playing political games while our families and communities are counting on us.

I’ll keep fighting to protect https://t.co/WBPgXZHa8R

At Marine Corps Training Area Bellows, I met with MCBH leadership to learn more about their stewardship of local waterways and how they balance critical military training with their responsibility to our ʻāina and surrounding communities.

Mahalo to the MCBH team for walking me https://t.co/EBnMoj8oeo

Congress’s first priority should be to the American people.

Whether it’s ending the war in Iran, the high cost of living, or holding this administration accountable for corruption, our communities and the people across our country have made it clear: America is ready for https://t.co/JPN9z0daMX

What makes a hospital special isn’t just the building. It’s the people inside.

Couldn’t think of a better way to kick off Rural Health Month than joining the blessing of Kohala Hospital’s new administrative wing, making more room for patients and families.

Mahalo to the https://t.co/BcK5yuG3TF

Big Oil is raking in huge profits while Hawaiʻi families pay the price.

Proud to stand with the Sierra Club against the so-called Stop Climate Shakedowns Act, which would shield fossil fuel corporations from accountability and leave our people footing the bill.

Our communities deserve their day in court, and our keiki deserve a future worth fighting for.

Today is Election Day!

Every vote matters, and every voice deserves to be heard.

Drop off your ballot at an official drop box or voter service center, or vote in person by 7 p.m. You can find your nearest polling location at https://t.co/epeo0ebpZp.

A big mahalo to our election workers and volunteers across the islands for all they do to keep our democracy strong.

Mahalo to Roots Reborn for bringing our Maui ʻohana together to celebrate Día de los Muertos and honor the loved ones we lost in the Lahaina fires.

Though they are no longer with us, we will carry their memories, celebrate their lives, and continue forward guided by the love they left behind.

They will always be part of Lahaina.

Mahalo to Hawaiian Community Assets for meeting with me in Hilo to discuss the Trump administration’s attempts to cut HUD housing counseling funding.

From preventing foreclosures to helping families achieve homeownership, their work is vital to our communities. I’ll keep https://t.co/zcIN5z4TVr

Congratulations to Hilo’s inaugural Pre-Apprenticeship Construction Training graduates!

PACT opens door to construction careers through hands-on experience and apprenticeship preparation—helping our young people build a good career, raise a family, and stay right here at home. https://t.co/SqqI2G7dpg

Mahalo to the Native Hawaiian Organizations Association (NHOA) for bringing together so many dedicated businesses and community partners for their Annual Community Showcase.

Native Hawaiian organizations do so much to uplift our communities, create opportunities, and give back to our people. I’m grateful for all that you do and will keep fighting to protect the programs and opportunities that help our communities thrive.

Visiting PACT Head Start in Hilo and Kona was a powerful reminder of what these programs mean for our keiki and families. From helping children find their voices to building stronger communities, Head Start changes lives for generations.

As the Trump administration threatens its https://t.co/iAFVE4gNMP

One step closer to home for more Maui families recovering from the wildfires. ❤️

Through the federally funded Hoʻokumu Hou program, 18 more families can take the next step toward finding a place to call home, with up to $600,000 in assistance. That brings the total to 100 families moving closer to rebuilding their lives on Maui.

Mahalo to Maui County and our partners for continuing to fight for the resources our families need to rebuild, put down roots, and remain home on Maui.

Mahalo to Hawaiʻi Farmers Union for bringing us together in Waimānalo for your 16th Annual Convention.

Our family farmers deserve better. We must undo the harm caused by federal cuts, tariffs & rising costs. And we have to unrig a system that favors big corporations over family https://t.co/APxPAQ5sU3

Congratulations to the Ilocos Surian Association of Maui on 22 years of service to our Filipino community.

Honored to celebrate this milestone, the first Miss Teen Ilocos Surian Maui coronation, and the honoring of outstanding leaders and members.

From supporting families to investing in our keiki through scholarships, your work carries forward the spirit of the sakadas who helped build Hawaiʻi 120 years ago. Mahalo for keeping our community and culture strong. 

Mabuhay!

At the 4th Annual Hawaiʻi Island Healthcare Conference, we discussed the growing challenges facing rural health care, from rising costs and threats to Medicaid coverage to local providers struggling to keep their doors open.

Behind every one of these challenges are our keiki, https://t.co/yCo8w2Sj37

REMINDER: Today is the last day to apply for a Military Service Academy Nomination with my office. All documents must be received today at 11:59 p.m. HST. For more info on application submissions, please visit https://t.co/G8HDyZwqA0 or contact my office at (808) 746-6220. https://t.co/sxcmuFtiBZ

Reflecting back on the I'm a Bright Kid Foundation 10 year celebration and all the classmates, friends, former teachers and amazing performers that filled the evening with love, laughter and song. When Mr B left us, it felt like a light had gone out in the world. To Aunty Mo and all the Bright Kids who made IABK possible, mahalo for turning the lights back on and inspiring generations of new Bright Kids who are lighting up our world. ❤️

When Hawaiʻi needs help, @hgeahawaii members are always there. From keeping our hospitals running to helping families through emergencies, our public workers show up for us every day.

It meant so much to join HGEA’s 28th Biennial General Assembly and thank them for all they do for our communities.

HGEA, you’ve always had my back and Hawaiʻi’s back. I promise I’ll always have yours.

Despite all the North Shore has been through, this community continues to show up for each other.

Mahalo to Lei for taking me through Wainiha, to Stacy and the team at Waipā for feeding families and building resilience, to Joel and the Hanalei Initiative for helping repair homes, and to Limahuli and everyone working to clear waterways and keep communities safe.

There’s still a lot of work ahead, but I left inspired by the aloha, strength, and care people continue to give one another.

At UH Mānoa, I heard directly from students, faculty, and staff about what the Trump Administration’s latest cuts to higher education funding mean for Hawaiʻi.

These cuts threaten critical-language programs, Asia-Pacific studies, and Hawaiʻi’s ability to build the relationships and cultural understanding that strengthen our security across the Pacific. Congress approved this funding—the administration has no right to withhold it.

I’ll keep fighting to protect UH, our students, and Hawaiʻi’s role as a bridge to the Pacific.

Mahalo to everyone who spoke up about what’s at stake.

Mahalo to the students, faculty, and staff at UH Maui College for inviting me to talk story over pizza. 🍕

We had a thoughtful conversation about the issues on their minds, from AI and the growing power of big tech to women's health and reproductive rights and school voucher court decisions. I’m always grateful for the chance to be with our students, hear what they’re thinking, and talk about the challenges shaping their lives and our communities.

Holding ICE accountable means knowing where taxpayer dollars are going and making sure the rule of law applies.

At Hawaiʻi’s first Immigration and Inclusion Conference, I shared what I’ve seen at FDC Honolulu and why Congress must keep pushing for answers, oversight, and humane treatment.

That means warrants, body cameras, no facial coverings, and a system where immigrants can live, work, and move through our communities without fear.

Mahalo to everyone standing up for the dignity and rights of our immigrant communities.

Was great to start the week in Hilo where I was able to meet up with Mayor Alameda & talk with Hawaiʻi Island elected officials about funding and executing storm/disaster recovery and how we can be better prepared for the next one.

As we face changes to how providers are reimbursed by local insurance carriers and the federal government, it was important for me to meet with independent healthcare providers from Hilo, Kona, and Waimea and talk about how we keep local practices open, strengthen our workforce, and sustain critical care in our communities, from internal medicine to radiology and mammography services.

Mahalo to our healthcare heroes for sharing what they’re seeing and what their patients need. These conversations help make sure Hawaiʻi’s needs are heard in Washington.

Chris Leonard and the team @KWXX know how important it is to keep people informed when the power is out, cell service is down, and families are looking for reliable information. 

Mahalo to the broadcasters who stay on air for our communities when it matters most. I’m working in Congress to make sure communications infrastructure is treated like the critical infrastructure it is.

Storm fatigue is real, but with Hurricane Nolo approaching Hawaiʻi, we can’t let our guard down. Now is the time to make sure you and your ʻohana are prepared and know where to get the latest information.

For current weather, shelters, alerts, and emergency updates:

• https://t.co/k0f2b8QOtN
• https://t.co/TVPWzxC2iM
• https://t.co/sWGN4P8WQu
• https://t.co/3akxOGVY1L
• https://t.co/3HDi8kLBa5
• https://t.co/JoyuRWqhMo

Please stay safe, check on your neighbors, and follow guidance from local emergency officials as conditions change.

As our islands prepare for another storm, Kauaʻi is still recovering from the last one.

Destroyed crops, damaged property, and ponds of dead shrimp have devastated Aloun Farms, Kauaʻi Shrimp, and Lydgate Farms. Kauaʻi Shrimp is now closing its operations, underscoring how devastating these losses are for local agriculture and the families and workers who depend on it.

Seeing the damage firsthand and talking with these farmers and UH CTAHR’s agriculture team made clear that recovery will take more than rebuilding, we need to also strengthen our agricultural resilience so our farmers aren’t left to shoulder catastrophic losses in future storms.

Glad to join the blessing of the MEERA lab at Mililani High School. This new space gives students hands-on experience with the equipment and technology used in manufacturing and engineering careers, helping them explore what their future could look like.

I’m proud to support initiatives like these that open up career pathways here in Hawaiʻi. Mahalo to the educators and partners making these opportunities possible for our keiki.

Mahalo to Mālama Mākua and the Waiʻanae Moku Kūpuna Council for bringing folks together to talk about the collective vision for the future of Mākua. 

A plan for the cleanup, return, and community-driven stewardship of Mākua is needed to ensure future generations can inherit and care for a healthier, more vibrant valley.

Governor Ariyoshi made history as our nation’s first Asian American governor, but I’ll remember him most for the humility, steady leadership, and deep love for Hawaiʻi that defined his service. 

My deepest aloha to Jean and the entire Ariyoshi ʻohana. Mahalo for a lifetime of service to Hawaiʻi, Governor.

Nobody wants explosive diarrhea. So why gamble with food safety?

The USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service has lost 860 positions—12% of its staff—and the FDA has lost over 800 food safety personnel. How are we supposed to build confidence in American food while losing the people who help keep it safe?

A lot of talk about growing markets for American agriculture. A whole lot of silence when I asked a simple question: who replaces the billions cut from SNAP and other programs that buy food from local farmers and ranchers?

That money doesn’t disappear on paper. It disappears from farmers’ bottom lines and families’ food baskets.

Farmers lose customers. Families lose food. That's the Republican plan for growing American agriculture.

I took to the House floor to share the stories of Japanese citizens abducted by North Korea and raise awareness for the families still waiting for answers.

Seventeen people are officially recognized as having been abducted. Five returned home. Twelve remain unaccounted for. We must keep their stories alive and continue standing with the families who are still waiting for answers.

When Hurricane Lowell hit, one of the only voices Kauaʻi could still hear was KKCR, their community radio station.

Through power and internet outages, KKCR stayed on the air, sharing emergency updates and helping people find food, water, and help. After Trump pushed Republicans to cut public broadcasting funding, KKCR lost $83,000. Congress must restore funding for this critical lifeline  because when disaster strikes and every other line of communication goes dark, Kauaʻi needs KKCR to be there.

This weekend I joined our community for the Lights for Lahaina Light March to remember to celebrate Maui’s resilience and aloha.

Across our islands, I’ve seen Maui ʻohana showing up for communities facing disasters, even as they continue their own recovery. That aloha reminds us that our people and our connection to each other is the true light of our state.

Mahalo to Aloha Amplified, the volunteers and sponsors, and especially the students who helped light the way.

From Kekaha to the North Shore, I traveled across Kaua'i to see the damage firsthand and check in with families, farmers, and community leaders.

Mahalo to every first responder, volunteer, airport worker, and neighbor who stepped up. I'll keep working to make sure Kaua'i has the support it needs to recover and rebuild.

The destruction Hurricane Lala left behind on farms across Kaʻū is extensive. From ranch lands to coffee farms, cracks in the earth, flooding, downed trees, broken water lines and damaged roads will take significant resources.

I’m working to urgently bring federal support to help our farmers recover and rebuild. Mahalo to USDA Farm Service Agency State Director Arthur Keyes and team for joining me as we spoke with local ranchers and farmers, surveyed the damage, and talked about what we can do to help.

Aloha and Haitai! With an andagi in hand, my belly was happy and my heart was full celebrating the 44th annual Okinawan Festival and 75 years of the Hawaiʻi United Okinawa Association.

As a proud yonsei of uchinanchu descent, I also had a great time talking story with the young leaders of the Okinawa Youth Academy who were helping out at the festival.

Ippe nifee debiru and Mahalo to the hundreds of volunteers keeping our heritage and the spirit of Chimugukuru alive across Hawaiʻi. ❤️

West Maui knew it could not wait to strengthen its fire and emergency response. The community donated the land. Raised $3 million. Fully funded a new fire station.

Then Trump's steel tariffs added more than $300,000 to the cost. It's time for Congress to exercise its constitutional authority over tariffs. We should be making communities safer, not making safety more expensive.

Three years after the fires, Lahaina families are finally coming home. They should be welcomed back, not told they will never have mail delivery at their rebuilt homes. Permanently closing the Downtown Lahaina Post Office without meaningful community input only adds insult to injury. 

Our message to USPS is simple: Lahaina has already lost enough. Restore meaningful mail service. Listen to the community. Don’t take another piece of Lahaina away.

Honored to join DHHL’s West Oʻahu Scattered Lots Pilot Project in Waiʻanae and celebrate another step toward getting Native Hawaiian families back on Hawaiian Home Lands.

These homes are about so much more than a roof. They’re about community, culture, and giving generations to come the chance to call Hawaiʻi home.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
